boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Rochester Institute of Technology
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe food and convenience destinations with currently published late hours, centered on campus and the Henrietta/Rochester area.

cards.title: Midnight Oil
cards.subtitle: Global Village, RIT campus
cards.notes: Head to Global Village for coffee, specialty drinks, sandwiches, desserts, and pastries; check the published weekly schedule before going.
cards.short_summary: A campus coffee-and-snack stop with fall-semester weeknight hours through 11 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT Dining lists Midnight Oil in Global Village and publishes Monday–Friday fall-semester hours ending at 11:00 p.m. for multiple weeks.
cards.access_notes: Published fall-semester schedules show Monday–Friday service until 11:00 p.m.; schedules vary by week and academic break.

cards.title: The Corner Store
cards.subtitle: RIT campus
cards.notes: Use this campus convenience-store stop for essentials and packaged items, and confirm the week shown on RIT Dining’s schedule.
cards.short_summary: A campus convenience option scheduled until midnight during many fall-semester weeks.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT Dining publishes The Corner Store’s fall-semester hours as 8:30 a.m.–12:00 a.m. on weekdays and 10:00 a.m.–12:00 a.m. on weekends for multiple weeks.
cards.access_notes: Published fall-semester schedules include midnight closing; hours change during breaks and special periods.

cards.title: Wendy’s on Jefferson Road
cards.subtitle: 566 Jefferson Rd, Rochester, NY 14623
cards.notes: Use the Jefferson Road location for a late food or drive-thru stop; verify holiday exceptions before making a trip.
cards.short_summary: Restaurant and drive-thru hours are listed until 3 a.m. daily.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy’s official location page lists both restaurant and drive-thru hours of 10:00 a.m.–3:00 a.m. every day at 566 Jefferson Rd.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists restaurant and drive-thru service until 3:00 a.m. daily; holiday hours may vary.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Jefferson Road
cards.subtitle: 950 Jefferson Rd, Rochester, NY 14623
cards.notes: Choose the drive-thru when dining-room service has ended, and check the location page for any short-notice schedule changes.
cards.short_summary: A Jefferson Road drive-thru listed until 3 a.m. every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell’s official page for 950 Jefferson Rd lists drive-thru hours from 7:00 a.m. to 3:00 a.m. daily and dine-in hours until 10:00 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru is published until 3:00 a.m. daily; dine-in is listed until 10:00 p.m.

cards.title: East of Chicago Henrietta
cards.subtitle: 4011 West Henrietta Road, Rochester, NY 14623
cards.notes: Place a carryout order through the restaurant’s online ordering page and use its posted schedule to confirm the closing time.
cards.short_summary: A West Henrietta Road pizza carryout option whose ordering page lists service until 1 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: East of Chicago Henrietta’s ordering page lists its address at 4011 West Henrietta Road and Sunday hours of 8:15 a.m.–1:00 a.m.
cards.source_title: East of Chicago Henrietta Online Ordering
cards.access_notes: The official ordering page lists hours through 1:00 a.m.; check the live ordering page before traveling.

cards.title: Henrietta Hots
cards.subtitle: 4018 West Henrietta Road, Rochester, NY 14623
cards.notes: Plan a late meal on Wednesday through Saturday, when the restaurant publishes midnight closing; confirm hours on the day.
cards.short_summary: A West Henrietta Road restaurant open until midnight Wednesday through Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Henrietta Hots’ official site lists Wednesday–Saturday hours of 11 a.m.–12 a.m. at 4018 West Henrietta Road.
cards.access_notes: Official hours list midnight closing Wednesday–Saturday; Monday and Tuesday close at 11 p.m. and Sunday at 10 p.m.

cards.title: DQ Grill & Chill on Jefferson Road
cards.subtitle: 1100 Jefferson Rd, Rochester, NY 14623
cards.notes: Check the posted day-specific hours before leaving; this location lists both dine-in and drive-thru late on Fridays and Saturdays.
cards.short_summary: A Jefferson Road food-and-treat stop with Friday and Saturday hours through 1 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Dairy Queen’s official location page lists Friday and Saturday store, drive-thru, and dine-in hours of 10:00 a.m.–1:00 a.m. at 1100 Jefferson Rd.
cards.source_title: DQ Grill & Chill Restaurant, 1100 Jefferson Rd
cards.access_notes: Official page lists dine-in and drive-thru until 1:00 a.m. Friday and Saturday, and until midnight Sunday–Thursday.

cards.title: Gourmet Hots
cards.subtitle: 295 East Ridge Road, Rochester, NY 14621
cards.notes: For a farther Rochester run, use the contact page’s listed hours and arrange transportation before heading across the city.
cards.short_summary: A Rochester food stop whose official page lists daily hours until 2 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Gourmet Hots’ official contact page lists its address at 295 East Ridge Road and hours of 11:00 a.m.–2:00 a.m. Monday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists daily closing at 2:00 a.m.; it is a Rochester destination farther from RIT than the Henrietta stops.

cards.title: Pizza Hut on East Henrietta Road
cards.subtitle: 2177 E Henrietta Rd, Rochester, NY 14623
cards.notes: Use carryout or delivery on Friday or Saturday, and verify the specific service mode and posted closing time before ordering.
cards.short_summary: An East Henrietta Road pizza option with Friday and Saturday carryout hours until midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza Hut’s official location page lists carryout hours at 2177 E Henrietta Rd until 12:00 a.m. Friday and 12:01 a.m. Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists carryout until midnight Friday and 12:01 a.m. Saturday; weekday hours are earlier.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Mount Hope Avenue
cards.subtitle: 1737 Mount Hope Avenue, Rochester, NY 14620
cards.notes: For a farther city option, use the official location page to confirm drive-thru availability and transportation before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: A Mount Hope Avenue Taco Bell listed as open until 3 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell’s official 950 Jefferson Rd page identifies the nearby 1737 Mount Hope Avenue Taco Bell as open until 3:00 a.m.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell Restaurant Near Me, 950 Jefferson Rd
cards.access_notes: The official Taco Bell page lists the Mount Hope Avenue location as open until 3:00 a.m.; confirm service details directly before travel.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named RIT spaces for making, studying, seeing creative work, gathering, and recreational activity.

cards.title: Student Alumni Union
cards.subtitle: Campus Center and student-life spaces
cards.notes: Use the lounges or game rooms to meet between classes, then check the union calendar or Campus Life listings for student-focused events.
cards.short_summary: A campus gathering point with lounges, games, dining, and events.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT describes the Student Alumni Union as having lounges, game rooms, dining options, and events for students.
cards.source_title: The Best Spots to Hang Out at RIT
cards.access_notes: Campus services and event access may vary; consult the relevant RIT office or event listing.

cards.title: MAGIC Spell Studios
cards.subtitle: Media-production and academic-lab facility
cards.notes: If you are working on media or design, review the listed facilities and contact MAGIC before planning a production or reserving specialized space.
cards.short_summary: A 52,000-square-foot studio and academic laboratory with production resources.
cards.evidence_claim: MAGIC states that its facilities are available for faculty, staff, and students and lists studios, labs, theater, and production spaces.
cards.access_notes: Facility use and bookings are arranged through MAGIC; specialized spaces are not walk-in public study areas.

cards.title: Wallace Library Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Wallace Library, 90 Lomb Memorial Drive
cards.notes: Reserve an individual or group room through RIT’s reservation system for studying, calls, or video conferencing; bring your RIT ID for access.
cards.short_summary: Reservable study rooms for focused solo or group work.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT Libraries says Wallace Library study rooms may be reserved for studying, phone/video calls, or video conferencing.
cards.access_notes: Advance EMS reservation and an RIT ID card are required; availability and after-hours access depend on staffing.

cards.title: The SHED
cards.subtitle: Student Hall for Exploration and Development
cards.notes: Walk through the atrium and courtyard, or connect a class, project team, maker activity, rehearsal, or performance plan to the building’s spaces.
cards.short_summary: A campus hub bringing technology, art, design, performance, and project spaces together.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT says the SHED houses makerspaces, project-team spaces, dance studios, rehearsal rooms, and performing-arts theaters.
cards.access_notes: Specific rooms and equipment can have course, program, reservation, or event restrictions.

cards.title: SHED Individual Practice Rooms
cards.subtitle: The SHED music-practice spaces
cards.notes: Bring your student ID and use an open practice period for solo singing or instrument work; check the current room-use guidance before arriving.
cards.short_summary: Private practice rooms intended for student music-making.
cards.evidence_claim: An RIT admissions article states that SHED individual practice rooms have open hours available to all majors with a student ID.
cards.source_title: RIT Beyond Studies: A Guide to Campus Life & Activities
cards.access_notes: Open hours and room availability may change; student ID is identified by RIT as required.

cards.title: University Gallery
cards.subtitle: James E. Booth Hall, Room 2700
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition listing before going, then use the gallery’s Booth Hall location details to plan a visit or a group tour.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus exhibition space for work by RIT and visiting artists and designers.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT identifies University Gallery as an exhibition space in Booth Hall showcasing professional alumni, faculty, and national and international artists and designers.
cards.access_notes: Exhibitions, group tours, and special events may have separate schedules or reservation requirements.

cards.title: Bevier Gallery
cards.subtitle: College of Art and Design, Booth Hall
cards.notes: Look for the current rotating exhibition and allow time to view student, faculty, alumni, or visiting-artist work in this on-campus gallery.
cards.short_summary: A College of Art and Design venue with changing creative-work exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT describes Bevier Gallery as its main on-campus College of Art and Design exhibition venue, with rotating creative-work shows.
cards.source_title: Galleries | College of Art and Design | RIT
cards.access_notes: Exhibition availability varies with the academic calendar and installation schedule.

cards.title: Red Barn Climbing
cards.subtitle: West end of campus
cards.notes: Complete the required release and bring proper ID, then follow Red Barn Climbing’s safety rules before using the bouldering gym.
cards.short_summary: An indoor bouldering facility that also houses Outdoor Education programs.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT says the Red Barn is a bouldering-only gym with padded falls and routes maintained for beginner through expert skill levels.
cards.source_title: Red Barn | Recreation and Wellness | RIT
cards.access_notes: RIT community access requires proper ID and an annual release; visitors may not climb or spot.

cards.title: RIT Tennis Courts
cards.subtitle: Near U-Lot
cards.notes: Bring a partner and appropriate equipment for a casual game, while checking recreation schedules for availability around intramurals or campus events.
cards.short_summary: Nine lighted outdoor courts used for recreation, wellness, intramurals, and events.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT states that its tennis courts near U-Lot are used for athletics, wellness, recreation, intramurals, and major campus events.
cards.access_notes: Court use can be affected by recreation schedules, reservations, intramurals, and major campus events.

cards.title: The Quads
cards.subtitle: RIT outdoor campus spaces
cards.notes: Use a blanket, book, or a small group meet-up outdoors, and watch campus announcements for activities that take place in these open areas.
cards.short_summary: Open campus areas used for relaxing, studying, and campus events.
cards.evidence_claim: An RIT admissions article describes the Quads as outdoor spaces for relaxing, studying, and participating in campus events.
cards.source_title: The Best Spots to Hang Out at RIT
cards.access_notes: Outdoor conditions and event setups affect use; follow posted campus-event guidance.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-admission, no-purchase ways to spend time on campus and in Rochester.

cards.title: See rotating work at Bevier Gallery
cards.subtitle: Booth Hall 2600, RIT campus
cards.notes: Stop in during weekday gallery hours to look through the current exhibition, then use the posted artist and show details to guide your conversation.
cards.short_summary: A free RIT campus gallery with rotating student, faculty, alumni, and visiting-artist work.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT states that Bevier Gallery is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Bevier Gallery | College of Art and Design | RIT
cards.access_notes: Open to the public Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; closed on weekends, RIT holidays/breaks, and during installations.

cards.title: Browse RIT City Art Space
cards.subtitle: 32 Adventure Place, downtown Rochester
cards.notes: Meet at the first-floor gallery and move through the exhibition together; check the gallery page before leaving because installations and breaks can close it.
cards.short_summary: RIT’s downtown exhibition venue presents art and design programming without an entry charge.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT says City Art Space exhibitions, events, and educational programming are free and open to the public year-round.
cards.source_title: About Us | City Art Space | RIT
cards.access_notes: The visit page lists summer hours Wednesday–Thursday 1–5 p.m., Friday–Saturday 1–8 p.m., and Sunday 1–5 p.m.; verify the current exhibition schedule.

cards.entity_name: RIT Nature Trails and Jogging Routes
cards.title: Walk the RIT Nature Trails
cards.subtitle: Wooded area by the Quarter Mile, south of the Student Life Center
cards.notes: Choose the measured 0.5- or 1.2-mile route and pause at The Bower; bring water and use the route PDF if you want a more deliberate walk.
cards.short_summary: Two measured woodland jogging routes on the RIT campus.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT describes 0.5-mile and 1.2-mile nature-trail routes adjacent to the Quarter Mile.
cards.source_title: Nature Trails and Jogging Routes | RIT Recreation and Wellness
cards.access_notes: Use the designated trails and check conditions before visiting; the page provides a downloadable trail and campus-jogging-routes PDF.

cards.title: Build a self-guided art-on-campus browse
cards.subtitle: RIT Libraries online exhibit
cards.notes: Pick an artist, artwork type, collection, or location from the archive, then compare a few entries and save a short list for a later campus walk.
cards.short_summary: A publicly accessible RIT Archives gallery of campus artworks.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT identifies Art on Campus as a publicly accessible gallery that can be browsed by artist, type, collection, and location.
cards.source_title: Online archive proves there’s plenty in a name | RIT
cards.access_notes: Available online; no campus entry or purchase is needed to browse the exhibit.

cards.title: Register for Film+FotoFest@RIT
cards.subtitle: MAGIC Spell Studios, September 16–17, 2026
cards.notes: Register when the form is posted, then make a plan to browse the trade-show floor, watch demos, and catch presentations with a friend.
cards.short_summary: A scheduled RIT photography and cinematography showcase with demos, exhibits, and talks.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT states that attendee registration for Film+FotoFest@RIT is free and open to the RIT community and public.
cards.source_title: Film+FotoFest@RIT | College of Art and Design | RIT
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for September 16–17, 2026; RIT says the registration form is forthcoming, so confirm details before attending.

cards.title: Explore Maplewood Nature Center
cards.subtitle: 107 Bridge View Drive, Rochester
cards.notes: Start with the interactive exhibits, then take the accessible trails through the gardens and use the birdwatching windows or riverway connection at your pace.
cards.short_summary: A city nature center with indoor exhibits, accessible trails, gardens, and a riverway-trail connection.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Rochester lists free admission for Maplewood Nature Center.
cards.source_title: Maplewood Nature Center | City of Rochester, New York
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Friday 9 a.m.–4 p.m. and Saturday 9 a.m.–2 p.m.; the City also lists free parking and accessible trails.

cards.title: Look through the City Hall Link Gallery
cards.subtitle: First floor, Rochester City Hall, 30 Church Street
cards.notes: Use the first-floor corridor between City Hall buildings as a short art stop, then take time to look closely at the current work by regional artists.
cards.short_summary: A Rochester City Hall gallery that displays work by artists and craftspeople from the region.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Rochester states that admission to the Link Gallery is free.
cards.source_title: City Hall's Link Gallery | City of Rochester, New York
cards.access_notes: Open to the public Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; closed Saturday and Sunday.

cards.title: Play a casual tennis set at Genesee Valley Park
cards.subtitle: 131 Elmwood Avenue, Rochester
cards.notes: Bring racquets and balls, then claim an available court on a first-come basis for a low-key rally, set, or rotating doubles game.
cards.short_summary: Eight outdoor tennis courts in Genesee Valley Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Rochester lists eight tennis courts at Genesee Valley Park and says its outdoor courts are free to use first-come, first-served.
cards.source_title: Tennis and pickleball courts | City of Rochester, New York
cards.access_notes: Courts are public and free on a first-come, first-served basis; a reservation is only needed to guarantee a selected court.

cards.title: Rally at Cobb's Hill Park
cards.subtitle: 80 Culver Road, Rochester
cards.notes: Pack basic tennis gear and use an open court for a rally or short set; coordinate a start time but expect first-come public use.
cards.short_summary: Six outdoor tennis courts at Cobb's Hill Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Rochester lists six tennis courts at Cobb's Hill Park and says its outdoor courts are free to use first-come, first-served.
cards.source_title: Tennis and pickleball courts | City of Rochester, New York
cards.access_notes: Courts are public and free on a first-come, first-served basis; a reservation is only needed to guarantee a selected court.

cards.title: Set up a pickleball game at Maplewood Park
cards.subtitle: 89 Maplewood Drive, Rochester
cards.notes: Bring paddles and a ball, choose an open court, and keep the game flexible so others can join or rotate through the six courts.
cards.short_summary: Six city pickleball courts in Maplewood Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Rochester lists six pickleball courts at Maplewood Park and says its outdoor courts are free to use first-come, first-served.
cards.source_title: Tennis and pickleball courts | City of Rochester, New York
cards.access_notes: Courts are public and free on a first-come, first-served basis; a reservation is only needed to guarantee a selected court.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on Calkins, Jefferson, East Henrietta, and Martin roads in RIT’s Henrietta-area orbit, each with a documented reason to stop.

cards.title: Veterans Memorial Park for the fitness trail
cards.subtitle: Calkins Road corridor
cards.notes: Use the Calkins Road entrance to reach the 3/4-mile fitness trail, then continue to the park’s Lehigh Valley Trail connection.
cards.short_summary: A town park with a fitness trail and trail connection.
cards.evidence_claim: Veterans Memorial Park at 595 Calkins Road has a 3/4-mile fitness trail and access to the Lehigh Valley Trail.
cards.access_notes: Town page lists park hours as 7 a.m.–10 p.m., seven days a week.

cards.title: Henrietta Public Library for a community-room stop
cards.subtitle: Calkins Road corridor
cards.notes: Check the library calendar before heading over; its Community Room hosts the public Library Board meetings listed by the town.
cards.short_summary: A municipal-complex library with a documented community meeting room.
cards.evidence_claim: Henrietta Public Library is at 625 Calkins Road, and the town lists Library Board meetings in its Community Room.
cards.access_notes: Verify library hours and individual program availability before visiting.

cards.title: Henrietta Recreation Center for scheduled activities
cards.subtitle: Calkins Road corridor
cards.notes: Look at the town recreation calendar for an activity that fits your visit; the center is the listed site for town youth programming.
cards.short_summary: A town recreation destination used for scheduled programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The Henrietta Recreation Center is at 605 Calkins Road and is the listed location for Youth Development Advisory Committee meetings.
cards.source_title: Youth Development Advisory Committee | Henrietta NY
cards.access_notes: Programs and entry requirements vary; check the town calendar first.

cards.title: Henrietta Town Hall for public-meeting access
cards.subtitle: Calkins Road corridor
cards.notes: Use the published Town Board schedule if you want to attend a civic meeting, and review the agenda before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A municipal meeting destination on Calkins Road.
cards.evidence_claim: Henrietta Town Hall is at 475 Calkins Road, and the town states that the public may speak at Town Board meetings.
cards.source_title: Contacting the Town Board | Henrietta NY
cards.access_notes: Meeting dates, rooms, and public-comment procedures can change; confirm with the town.

cards.title: Tinker Nature Park for its walking trails
cards.subtitle: Calkins Road corridor
cards.notes: Start from the Calkins Road side and choose either the 1.2-mile walking/exercise trail or the half-mile nature trail.
cards.short_summary: A 68-acre town nature park with two documented trail options.
cards.evidence_claim: Tinker Nature Park at 1525 Calkins Road has a 1.2-mile walking/exercise trail and a half-mile nature trail.
cards.access_notes: The town lists the park as open daily from 7 a.m. until dusk; pets are not permitted.

cards.title: Hansen Nature Center for natural-history displays
cards.subtitle: Calkins Road corridor at Tinker Nature Park
cards.notes: Pair a trail visit with the center’s New York natural-history displays, and arrive before the listed last-admission time.
cards.short_summary: A free-admission nature center within Tinker Nature Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Hansen Nature Center features New York natural-history displays, offers year-round classes, and states that admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Town page lists Tuesday–Saturday hours, 9 a.m.–4 p.m., with last admission at 3:45 p.m.

cards.title: Tinker Homestead for the cobblestone farm museum
cards.subtitle: Calkins Road corridor at Tinker Nature Park
cards.notes: Call ahead to arrange a tour, then focus on the restored homestead and farm implements that interpret regional agricultural change.
cards.short_summary: A restored 1830 cobblestone homestead and farm museum.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tinker Homestead & Farm Museum includes an 1830 cobblestone farm and displays farm implements; tours are available by appointment.
cards.source_title: Tinker Homestead & Farm Museum | Henrietta NY
cards.access_notes: Tours are listed by appointment Tuesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–2 p.m.; call before visiting.

cards.title: Lookup Park for disc golf and the dog park
cards.subtitle: East Henrietta Road corridor
cards.notes: Bring the gear appropriate to your plan: the town’s park listing identifies both a short disc-golf course and a dog park here.
cards.short_summary: A town park with short disc golf, dog-park, and driving-range amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: Lookup Park at 3850 East Henrietta Road is listed with a dog park, a short disc-golf course, and a golf driving range.
cards.access_notes: Confirm individual amenity conditions with Henrietta Parks and Recreation.

cards.title: Martin Road Park for courts and a fishing pond
cards.subtitle: Martin Road corridor
cards.notes: Choose a court, field, or the catch-and-release pond; the town specifically prohibits swimming in the pond.
cards.short_summary: An 80-acre town park with courts, fields, and catch-and-release fishing.
cards.evidence_claim: Martin Road Park at 1344 Martin Road has a catch-and-release fishing pond, soccer field, and tennis/pickleball courts.
cards.access_notes: Town page lists hours from 7 a.m. until sunset, seven days a week; no swimming in the pond.

cards.title: Genesee Valley Regional Market for its tenant directory
cards.subtitle: Jefferson Road corridor
cards.notes: Use the authority’s tenant directory to identify a specific business before you go; the market property is a large multi-tenant site.
cards.short_summary: A 190-company regional market property on Jefferson Road.
cards.evidence_claim: The Genesee Valley Regional Market Authority at 900 Jefferson Road reports that 190 companies do business on its Henrietta and Chili property.
cards.source_title: Genesee Valley Regional Market Authority | Rochester, NY
cards.access_notes: Authority contact page lists Monday–Friday hours of 7 a.m.–5 p.m.; individual tenants may differ.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: A year-round set of RIT’s officially identified campus traditions, from welcoming new Tigers to celebrating graduates.

cards.title: New Student Orientation
cards.subtitle: The pre-semester welcome series
cards.notes: Use the orientation schedule to meet campus resources and begin building connections before classes start; dates and activities are published by RIT.
cards.short_summary: RIT’s organized transition into campus life.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT identifies New Student Orientation as a series of events and activities that helps students and families transition to life at RIT before classes begin.
cards.access_notes: Dates vary annually; consult RIT’s orientation schedule.

cards.title: Tiger Walk
cards.subtitle: New Tigers’ procession to convocation
cards.notes: Watch for the annual first-year procession on the Quarter Mile, where campus community members cheer as new students head to Fall Convocation.
cards.short_summary: A spirited welcome procession for incoming students.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT says the first Tiger Walk was held in 2004 and describes faculty, staff, students, and family members cheering incoming students along the Quarter Mile.
cards.access_notes: Held as part of New Student Convocation; timing is set with fall orientation.

cards.title: TigerFest
cards.subtitle: First-week celebration of a new academic year
cards.notes: Browse the first-week program for activities that connect students with fellow Tigers, campus opportunities, and RIT’s student-life traditions.
cards.short_summary: RIT’s welcome festival for the start of classes.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT describes TigerFest as bringing the community together during the first week of classes to celebrate the start of a new academic year.
cards.access_notes: RIT lists TigerFest for Aug. 23–29, 2026; individual events vary.

cards.title: FallFest
cards.subtitle: RIT’s autumn seasonal celebration
cards.notes: Check the annual FallFest program for fall-themed events presented by campus departments, student clubs, and student organizations.
cards.short_summary: A campus-wide marker of the Rochester fall season.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT calls FallFest the kickoff to its annual seasonal celebrations and says it includes events sponsored by departments and student clubs and organizations.
cards.access_notes: RIT lists FallFest for Sept. 17–20, 2026; consult the event program.

cards.entity_name: Brick City Homecoming and Family Weekend
cards.title: Brick City Homecoming and Family Weekend
cards.subtitle: Families, alumni, and Tigers gather on campus
cards.notes: Review the weekend schedule for campus activities, including speakers, the Brick City 5K, and Tiger athletic events.
cards.short_summary: RIT’s annual homecoming and family gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT describes Brick City Homecoming and Family Weekend as a yearly tradition honoring families, students, alumni, staff, and friends of the university.
cards.access_notes: RIT lists the 2026 weekend as Oct. 16–18; individual activities have separate details.

cards.title: FreezeFest
cards.subtitle: The winter tradition with Roarie the white tiger
cards.notes: Bundle up and follow the multi-day FreezeFest calendar for winter activities; RIT highlights ice skating and visits from white tiger mascot Roarie.
cards.short_summary: A winter campus celebration built around cold-weather activities.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT calls FreezeFest a longstanding annual winter tradition with multiple days of festivities, including ice skating, and identifies Roarie as its white tiger mascot.
cards.access_notes: RIT lists FreezeFest for Jan. 31–Feb. 6, 2027; check the calendar for activities.

cards.title: SpringFest
cards.subtitle: Pre-finals spring celebration
cards.notes: See the SpringFest lineup before finals for music, games, food, and other RIT-programmed activities celebrating the end of the academic year.
cards.short_summary: A springtime pause before final exams.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT describes SpringFest as an end-of-academic-year spring celebration before finals with music, food, games, and free swag.
cards.access_notes: RIT lists SpringFest for April 15–18, 2027; event offerings vary.

cards.title: Imagine RIT
cards.subtitle: University-wide innovation and creativity showcase
cards.notes: Plan time to explore hands-on demonstrations, interactive presentations, performances, and exhibits created by RIT students, faculty, and staff.
cards.short_summary: An annual public showcase of work made across RIT.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT says Imagine RIT is a university-wide event with hundreds of exhibits, hands-on demonstrations, interactive presentations, and performances.
cards.access_notes: RIT lists Imagine RIT for April 24, 2027; consult the event site for exhibit details.

cards.title: Commencement
cards.subtitle: RIT’s final academic celebration
cards.notes: Graduating students can follow RIT’s commencement guidance for academic convocation, college ceremonies, and Grad Week events such as Passing the Torch.
cards.short_summary: The ceremonial close of an RIT degree.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT describes Commencement as the final chapter at RIT, including academic convocation, college ceremonies, and Grad Week events such as Passing the Torch.
cards.access_notes: RIT lists commencement for May 7–8, 2027; eligibility and ceremony details are published separately.

cards.title: ROAR Day
cards.subtitle: RIT’s annual day of giving
cards.notes: Follow RIT’s annual giving updates to support an RIT college, program, scholarship, or activity that matters to you.
cards.short_summary: A recurring campus-wide philanthropy tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT describes ROAR Day as an annual day of giving that lets the RIT community support areas of the university that enriched their experience.
cards.source_title: Tigers flex their philanthropic muscles on ROAR Day | RIT
cards.access_notes: Participation may involve making a gift; follow RIT’s current ROAR Day announcement.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Rochester Institute of Technology, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure, on-campus first-weekend route: orient yourself, find useful hubs, try an activity, and end at a game or event venue.

cards.title: Start at The Sentinel
cards.subtitle: Albert Paley sculpture at RIT’s main entrance
cards.notes: Meet here for a quick campus landmark photo, then walk through the open base before heading farther into the academic core.
cards.short_summary: Use RIT’s monumental entrance sculpture as a clear first waypoint.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT identifies The Sentinel as a 73-foot Albert Paley sculpture at the campus entrance; pedestrians can walk through its open bottom.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor artwork; observe from public campus walkways.

cards.title: Get oriented at Global Village
cards.subtitle: 6000 Reynolds Drive
cards.notes: Walk through the complex to locate dining, the market, shops, event spaces, and the post office for future reference.
cards.short_summary: A mixed-use campus hub for practical first-weekend errands and browsing.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT describes Global Village as a complex combining student living with dining, shopping, learning, and event spaces.
cards.access_notes: Businesses and services within the complex have separate hours and purchase requirements.

cards.title: Pause at Artesano Bakery & Café
cards.subtitle: Monroe Hall
cards.notes: Choose a pastry, sandwich, or coffee break if you want one, and use the stop to get familiar with Monroe Hall.
cards.short_summary: A campus bakery and café stop with sweet and savory food options.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT Dining lists Artesano Bakery & Café as a patisserie serving desserts, breakfast pastries, sandwiches, and coffee drinks.
cards.access_notes: Check RIT Dining’s live location page for the current operating schedule; payment is required for food and drinks.

cards.title: Learn Wallace Library’s layout
cards.subtitle: RIT Libraries’ main campus library
cards.notes: Find the room-reservation tools and map, then pick a study area or plan a later visit to the archives and collections.
cards.short_summary: A practical study-and-research anchor connected to campus academic life.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT Libraries provides a Wallace Library map and room-reservation access; its site also lists collections, archives, and digital resources.
cards.access_notes: Library services, spaces, and room availability may vary; use the library site before visiting.

cards.title: Find the Campus Center
cards.subtitle: Campus Life-managed student hub
cards.notes: Take a pass through to spot gathering areas and postings, then note it as a central place to check for student events.
cards.short_summary: A campus-life building for gatherings, lounges, meetings, and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT Campus Life lists the Campus Center among its core buildings and describes these spaces as offering gathering spots, lounges, meeting spaces, and dining.
cards.access_notes: RIT lists Campus Center building hours as 7 a.m.–midnight Monday–Thursday, with different weekend hours; break schedules can differ.

cards.title: Walk through the Student Alumni Union
cards.subtitle: Campus Life-managed building beside the hockey arena
cards.notes: Use the visit to locate its lounges, meeting areas, dining options, and the nearby entrance to the Gene Polisseni Center.
cards.short_summary: A student-life hub that combines gatherings, services, and food options.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT Campus Life identifies the Student Alumni Union as a core campus-life space with gathering spots, lounges, classrooms, meeting spaces, and dining.
cards.access_notes: RIT lists building hours as 7 a.m.–1 a.m. Friday and 8 a.m.–1 a.m. Saturday; individual businesses have separate schedules.

cards.entity_name: Kilian J. and Caroline F. Schmitt Interfaith Center
cards.title: Locate the Schmitt Interfaith Center
cards.subtitle: Campus Life-managed interfaith space
cards.notes: Add this building to your campus mental map and check its posted resources or programming when you want a quieter community stop.
cards.short_summary: An identifiable campus-life space included in RIT’s student-community facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT Campus Life lists the Kilian J. and Caroline F. Schmitt Interfaith Center among the spaces it oversees.
cards.access_notes: RIT’s listed building hours are 7 a.m.–midnight Monday–Thursday, with different weekend hours; observe any posted room-use guidance.

cards.title: Try Red Barn Climbing
cards.subtitle: 44 Lomb Memorial Drive
cards.notes: If you want an active stop, review the rules, bring required identification, and ask staff about a beginner-appropriate bouldering visit.
cards.short_summary: An indoor bouldering facility with routes for beginner through expert levels.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT says Red Barn Climbing is a bouldering-only gym with routes maintained for all abilities and is open to the RIT community and guests.
cards.access_notes: An annual release, proper ID, shirts, footwear, and climbing shoes are required; check the live facility page for current hours and fees.

cards.entity_name: Gordon Field House and Activities Center
cards.title: Find the Gordon Field House
cards.subtitle: RIT recreation and event facility
cards.notes: Check the recreation schedule before going, then use the building as a reference point for open recreation or a future campus event.
cards.short_summary: A large recreation facility directly attached to the Student Life Center.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT describes the Gordon Field House as a 160,000-square-foot facility directly attached to the Student Life Center and makes recreation facilities available to the RIT community.
cards.access_notes: Open recreation and reservations depend on the facility schedule; confirm current availability through Recreation and Wellness.

cards.title: End at the Gene Polisseni Center
cards.subtitle: 200 Lomb Memorial Drive
cards.notes: Check the venue calendar and ticket page for an upcoming men’s or women’s hockey game, then review the clear-bag policy before attending.
cards.short_summary: RIT’s on-campus arena and home venue for men’s and women’s hockey.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT identifies the Gene Polisseni Center as the home for men’s and women’s hockey games and a multi-purpose venue.
cards.access_notes: Events vary and tickets may be required; use the venue calendar and review its clear-bag policy before arrival.
